bug_description: Applying torch.nn.utils.weight_norm to nn.Linear(0, 1) and running a forward pass with an empty input triggers undefined behavior in the CPU weight_norm kernel. The Vectorized<float>::loadu function in aten/src/ATen/cpu/vec/vec256/vec256_float.h passes a null pointer to std::memcpy when the underlying tensor has zero elements (data pointer is nullptr). Specifically, when loadu is called with ptr=nullptr and count=0, it enters the partial-load path (count != size()) and executes std::memcpy(tmp_values, nullptr, 0). Passing a null pointer to memcpy is undefined behavior per the C/C++ standard, even when the byte count is zero. UBSan detects this as: runtime error: null pointer passed as argument 2, which is declared to never be null.
build_sh:
#!/bin/bash -eu
# Build the harness against the ACTUAL vec256_float.h from the PyTorch tree.
# Stub headers in /src/stubs/ provide:
#   - sleef.h       (function declarations for the Sleef math library)
#   - ATen/Config.h (build-time config, all features disabled)
#   - c10/macros/cmake_macros.h (empty, no optional features)
#   - torch/headeronly/macros/Export.h (empty export macros)
#
# All other headers come from the real PyTorch source at /src/pytorch/.

cd /src/pytorch

${CXX:-clang++} \
    -fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all \
    -std=c++17 -O1 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
    -DCPU_CAPABILITY_AVX2 -DCPU_CAPABILITY=AVX2 \
    -mavx2 -mfma \
    -I /src/stubs \
    -I /src/pytorch/aten/src \
    -I /src/pytorch \
    /src/harness.cpp \
    -o /src/harness_bin
secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    if /usr/local/bin/compile 1>/dev/null; then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR pytorch.issue-181510..."
    /src/harness_bin
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/pytorch
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi
dockerfile:
FROM hwiwonlee/secb.base:latest
ENV FUZZING_LANGUAGE=c++
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y git && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN git init /src/pytorch \
    && cd /src/pytorch \
    && git remote add origin https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch.git \
    && git fetch --depth 1 origin ba56102387ef21a3b04b357e5b183d48f0afefc7 \
    && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
RUN cd /src/pytorch \
    && rm -rf .git \
    && git init \
    && git config user.email "secbench@local" \
    && git config user.name "secbench" \
    && git add -A && git commit -m "pytorch at ba56102 (pre-patch)"
WORKDIR $SRC/pytorch
COPY stubs/ /src/stubs/
COPY harness.cpp $SRC/harness.cpp
COPY build.sh $SRC/
RUN mkdir -p /testcase
COPY poc.py /testcase/poc.py

bug_report:
================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/181510
## Description:
Issue: pytorch/pytorch#181510
Title: torch.nn.utils.weight_norm triggers a UBSan null pointer error for nn.Linear(0, 1) on CPU
State: open
Created at: 2026-04-27

Issue Body:
Applying torch.nn.utils.weight_norm to nn.Linear(0, 1) and then running a forward pass with an empty input triggers a UBSan runtime error in the CPU weight norm kernel:

aten/src/ATen/cpu/vec/vec256/vec256_float.h:124:16: runtime error: null pointer passed as argument 2, which is declared to never be null

A plain nn.Linear(0, 1) does not trigger this issue in the same ASAN/UBSAN build, so this looks specific to the weight_norm code path rather than zero-sized linear layers in general.

Minimal repro:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.nn.utils import weight_norm
m = nn.Linear(0, 1)
m = weight_norm(m)
x = torch.empty((1, 0), dtype=torch.float32)
print(m(x))

Stack trace:
#0 at::vec::AVX2::Vectorized<float>::loadu(void const*, long)
#1 map_reduce_all<...>
#2 weight_norm_first_dim_kernel<float, float>
#3 weight_norm_kernel
#4 at::native::weight_norm_cpu(...)

PyTorch version: 2.8.0a0+gitba56102
Git commit: ba56102387ef21a3b04b357e5b183d48f0afefc7
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
Reproduced on an ASAN/UBSAN build of PyTorch.
